claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by getting the first question in the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start with the first question:

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming for?**

Please tell me:
1. The child's name
2. Their age or date of birth

This will help me determine which eligibility path to follow. Child Benefit has different rules depending on whether the child is:
- **Under 16** years old
- **16-19 years old** (with additional requirements)
- **20 years old or over**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'd like to find out if I'm eligible for Child Benefit please. I have one child - Alex, who is 19 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, **Alex, who is 19 years old**.

Since Alex is in the 16-19 age group, I need to check some additional requirements. Let me get the next set of questions.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to understand Alex's current situation:

**Is Alex currently in education or training, or did he recently leave education?**

Please let me know:
- Is Alex currently attending school, college, or doing approved training?
- OR has Alex recently left education (within the last 20 weeks)?
- OR is Alex in neither of these situations?

This is important because for 16-19 year olds, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether they're in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is currently in college - he's studying for his A-levels.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So Alex is currently in college studying for A-levels. That means he's in approved education. Let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check the details of Alex's A-level course to make sure it meets the requirements for Child Benefit:

**Regarding Alex's A-level studies:**

1. **Is he studying full-time?** (This means at least 12 hours per week of supervised study time)

2. **Is the A-level course funded by an employer** (where you've agreed it's for a future job with them)?

3. **Is Alex married?** (If so, he would need to be financially dependent on you)

A-levels are generally approved education for Child Benefit purposes, but I need to confirm these details to make sure all the requirements are met.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's studying full-time - it's a regular sixth form college course. It's not funded by any employer, just the normal state-funded education. And no, he's not married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex's situation looks good so far. He's in approved full-time education (A-levels at a state-funded college), not married, and not employer-funded. Let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, now I need to check about Alex's work situation:

**Does Alex work, and if so, how many hours per week?**

For eligibility purposes, as long as Alex is in full-time approved education (which he is with his A-levels), he can work. However, I just need to confirm his work situation for our records.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't work, so that requirement is met. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit (in his own name)
- Any other state benefits claiming to be an independent applicant

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a student living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex isn't receiving any benefits in his own name. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now, one more question about Alex's current activity:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is studying A-levels at college (not an apprenticeship), I expect the answer is no. Just confirming to make sure there's no apprenticeship involved.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not doing an apprenticeship - just his A-levels at college as I mentioned.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is just doing his A-levels, so he's not in an apprenticeship. Now I need to check some details about you as the claimant.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation:

**Where do you normally live? Do you meet any of these residency requirements?**

The main residency paths are:

1. **Normally live in the UK** - This is the most straightforward route
2. **Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - If you're an EU/EEA citizen
3. **Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - With specific additional requirements (working, studying, jobseeking, or sufficient resources)
4. **Crown servant living abroad** - In specific qualifying countries

Could you tell me about your residency situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm based in Manchester and have been living here normally.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! You normally live in the UK, which means you meet the residency requirement. Let me move on to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and upkeep?**

You can meet this requirement if:
1. **You live with Alex** - which you mentioned you do (he lives at home with you)
2. OR you contribute to his upkeep (food, clothes, housing, etc.)
3. OR you pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

Since you mentioned Alex lives at home with you, it sounds like you meet this requirement. Can you confirm that you're living with Alex and supporting him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me and I support him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex and support him, so you meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else claimed it previously?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Has another guardian or relative claimed for him?
- Has this been claimed by someone else in the past?

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any one time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Good! So there's no other claimant for Alex. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Is Alex in any of these situations:**
- In hospital (for a long-term stay)?
- In local authority care?
- Being fostered?
- OR living normally at home with you?

Based on what you've told me (he lives at home with you and goes to college), I expect he's living normally at home. Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex is living normally at home with me. He's not in hospital, care, or being fostered.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
One final check:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

For example:
- Is the council paying for his housing?
- Is the council providing financial support for his care?

Generally, if the local council is paying for the child's upkeep, you wouldn't be eligible for Child Benefit. But if you're paying for Alex yourself (which it sounds like you are), then you should be fine.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm supporting him myself - he just lives at home with me and I cover all his costs.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You're supporting Alex yourself and the council isn't paying anything towards him. This means you've met all the eligibility requirements. Let me confirm the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex!

Great news! Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the eligibility requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

### Summary of Your Eligibility:

**Alex's Status:**
- **Age:** 19 years old (within the qualifying age range)
- **Education:** Full-time A-levels at state-funded college (approved education)
- **Work:** Not working (meets requirements)
- **Benefits:** Not receiving ESA or Universal Credit in his own right
- **Apprenticeship:** Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship

**Your Situation:**
- **Residency:** Normally resident in the UK (Manchester)
- **Responsibility:** Live with Alex and support him financially
- **Other Claimants:** No one else is claiming for Alex
- **Council Support:** The council is not paying towards his upkeep

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online** at gov.uk/child-benefit or **apply by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself (passport, driving licence, etc.)
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Important:** Be aware of the **High Income Child Benefit Charge** - if you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay some or all of it back through Self-Assessment
5. **Payment frequency:** Usually paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if applicable)

For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Good luck with your application!
